chunks: And in the narration of Ibn Faḍḍāl, from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

The diyah for a hunting dog is forty dirhams, and the diyah for a livestock dog is twenty dirhams. And the diyah for a dog that is neither for hunting nor for livestock is a basket of dirt; the killer must give it, and its owner must accept it.

key_terms.الْقَاتِلِ: The one who killed the animal and is liable to provide the compensation.
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: A silver coin used here as the unit of legal compensation.
key_terms.دِيَةُ كَلْبِ الصَّيْدِ: The legal compensation due for killing a hunting dog.
key_terms.دِيَةُ كَلْبِ الْمَاشِيَةِ: The legal compensation due for killing a dog used to guard livestock.
key_terms.زَبِيلٌ مِنْ تُرَابٍ: A basket of dirt, indicating merely nominal compensation.

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for killing a hunting dog, a livestock dog, or an ordinary dog in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal compensation values for killing different kinds of dogs, distinguishing between those with recognized use and those without. It assigns a higher diyah to a hunting dog, a lower one to a livestock dog, and only a token compensation for a dog with neither function.
